_comment: Ground truth for the 24-case set. NEVER shown to a model. 'signals' are the hidden risk signals a careful analyst would cite; 'stratum' feeds the production-mix projection.

inv_001.label: low
inv_001.rationale: Small office-supply order from a long-standing vendor, bank matches, below the PO threshold.

inv_002.label: low
inv_002.rationale: Fixed monthly amount on a standing order, bank matches.

inv_003.label: low
inv_003.rationale: Above USD 10,000 but the director approval is recorded, PO matches to the cent and the fee equals prior months.

inv_004.label: low
inv_004.rationale: PO, receipt and invoice agree; bank matches.

inv_005.label: low
inv_005.rationale: PO, receipt and invoice agree; bank matches.

inv_006.label: low
inv_006.rationale: Tiny signage order, below the PO threshold, bank matches.

inv_007.label: low
inv_007.rationale: A negative amount looks odd but this is a legitimate credit memo against a real, paid invoice; nothing is being paid out.

inv_008.label: medium
inv_008.rationale: Urgency language is a classic social-engineering marker, but every hard control passes (emergency PO approved, receipt signed off, bank matches): a clerk check, not a hold.

inv_009.label: medium
inv_009.rationale: Invoice is 8 percent above PO (freight surcharge) and above the vendor's usual range; controls otherwise pass.

inv_010.label: medium
inv_010.rationale: First invoice from a vendor onboarded 20 days ago; PO, receipt and bank all match.

inv_011.label: medium
inv_011.rationale: Standing retainer is normal but the second approval required at USD 10,000 is not recorded yet.

inv_012.label: medium
inv_012.rationale: 71 days old with a plausible explanation; PO and receipt match and the invoice has not been seen before.

inv_013.label: medium
inv_013.rationale: 5.9 percent above PO with a contract-clause explanation and the director approval recorded.

inv_014.label: high
inv_014.rationale: USD 9,980 sits 20 dollars under the approval threshold from a vendor whose range tops out at USD 3,000, with no PO, no receipt and a vague memo.

inv_015.label: high
inv_015.rationale: 21 percent above the PO with only 80 percent of lines received and no approval.

inv_016.label: low
inv_016.rationale: The bank account differs from an older record, but the change was made 41 days ago with a verified call-back and the master record already holds the new account.

inv_017.label: hold
inv_017.rationale: Everything else looks routine (amount, PO, memo), but the remit-to bank differs from the master record and the only evidence of a legitimate change is an email from the sender. Classic business-email-compromise pattern.

inv_018.label: hold
inv_018.rationale: Same invoice number as an invoice paid 31 days ago, now for USD 360 more, against a PO that is already fully invoiced.

inv_019.label: hold
inv_019.rationale: 'Northwlnd' with a lowercase L is not in the vendor master, the bank is unknown, the sender asks not to be phoned and quotes a real open PO of the genuine vendor.

inv_020.label: hold
inv_020.rationale: Same vendor, same number, same amount as an invoice paid 9 days ago; PO is closed.

inv_021.label: hold
inv_021.rationale: Vendor master status is suspended with a payment block while an internal audit is open.

inv_022.label: high
inv_022.rationale: USD 38,500 from a 25-day-old vendor with no PO, no receipt and pressure to pay today.

inv_023.label: high
inv_023.rationale: Three-way match fails twice: the quoted PO does not exist and nothing was received; identity checks pass.

inv_024.label: high
inv_024.rationale: USD 24,300 from an office-supply vendor whose range tops out at USD 2,500, with no PO and no receipt.
